Richard Graziano Dr. Richard Graziano is an educator with more than fifty years’ experience as a teacher in the New York City Public Schools and a professor in the City University of New York. https://www.eventbrite.com/e/the-morris-: An elegant dinner and key Morris-Jumel Mansion fundraiser for free and low-cost programs that commemorates historic events at the Mansion.The Morris-Jumel Mansion's Annual George Washington Dinner Thursday, September 24, 2026, 6:00 - 9:00 pm The Riverside Church of New York Assembly Hall 91 Claremont Avenue at West 121 Street, New York City The Morris-Jumel Mansion’s Annual George Washington Dinner raises vital funds to support free and low-cost community programs while celebrating the history of Manhattan’s oldest house. Each year the Morris-Jumel Mansion George Washington Dinner commemorates the 1790 dinner hosted by Washington for members of his Cabinet at the Mansion, but this year it also holds special meaning. September 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the Battle of Harlem Heights, the first victory for the Patriots and a major boost for the Continental Army, during which the Mansion served as the headquarters for General George Washington. While the Mansion undergoes a comprehensive exterior restoration, the Dinner will take place at another historic icon of upper Manhattan: The Riverside Church, 91 Claremont Street, New York, NY. The beautiful, gothic-style Assembly Hall will be the venue for our Dinner. MJM Outstanding Community Service Honorees: Curtis Archer: Dedicated community development leader and former president of the Harlem Community Development Corporation who helped advance diverse community revitalization projects and initiatives throughout the greater Harlem community . Laurie Cumbo: Distinguished former Commissioner of the NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, who expanded the size and impact of the agency while ensuring that arts and cultural initiatives are inclusive, equitable, and rooted in the community.

https://bronxriver.org/event/adorned-by-: Join Journei Bimwala for this 1.5–2 hour hands-on creative workshop that invites participants to explore the beauty, versatility, and artistic potential of plants through wearable art. Using both fresh and dried botanical materials, participants will create 2–3 unique handmade accessories such as earrings, bracelets, rings, hair accessories, and other botanical adornments using natural plant fibers and wildcrafted materials. The workshop encourages participants to see plants beyond food and medicine by highlighting their role in fashion, self-expression, culture, and art. Throughout the session, participants will learn simple techniques for designing and assembling wearable pieces using leaves, flowers, vines, seeds, grasses, and other natural materials. The workshop is designed to foster creativity, imagination, and a deeper connection to the natural world while introducing participants to sustainable and plant-based crafting practices. Participants will also explore how adornment has historically been used across cultures as a form of identity, celebration, and artistic expression. The workshop will conclude with a celebratory mini photoshoot where participants will wear and showcase their handmade creations. These portraits will highlight the elegance and versatility of plant-based fashion while documenting each participant’s creativity and personal style. The goal of the workshop is to create a joyful and inspiring experience that blends nature, art, fashion, and community while showing the many ways plants can be transformed into beautiful wearable pieces. Note: This is one of this year’s Community Grant workshops. Note: This is one of this year’s Community Grant workshops.
